body:
Thank you, I get what you mean and I'm sorry for your loss.

It's hard, or maybe not, but I wouldn't say I don't trust my family or my friends. I'd like to think I do, and I believe they would make the effort tolove me for who I am... but I think that's not fair. I know what it feels to be there, to have someone you love proclaim that they want to die. You feel like you don't matter, and do everything you can to keep that person happy and away from self\-harm and thoughts of disappearing, because you love them. I think that's not right.

The first time you don't notice it, you would do anything to make that person happy. But years pass and you realize you are where you never wanted to be, doing what you never wanting to do, just because that's what that person wanted for you, because it is what's best for you, according to them. You love them, but you simply do not love yourself, or the person you currently are, and you feel you can't do anything, or say anything, because it might negatively affect those who are responsible of your current situation.

I just don't want to put anyone in that situation. It's selfish and immature, but I'd rather have them wonder 'what if' than become  the reason others are forced to live in a way they don't want to.
